messages.content: Before you book the Fairfield, compare it cleanly with the Lincoln Square hotel. Include taxes, the local transportation we would actually use, and the Monday luggage issue.

For September 25–28, one king room for two adults, the Lincoln Square Hotel is $598 before tax and $624 total. Fairfield Inn & Suites Chicago Downtown/River North is $652 before tax and $711 total on the refundable rate. For transportation, I estimate $44 from the Lincoln Square property for the airport and downtown trips versus $30 for two three-day CTA passes from the Fairfield. That puts hotel plus local transit at $668 for Lincoln Square and $741 for Fairfield.
So Lincoln Square is $73 less for the room and $99 less after transportation?
Correct. The room difference is $87 after tax, and the estimated transportation difference narrows the full gap to $73: $668 versus $741. I had those two figures reversed in your question’s wording.
Thank you. Now check whether either has a problem with our late Friday arrival.

Fairfield has a staffed front desk around the clock, so the expected 11:15–11:35 p.m. arrival is covered as long as the reservation notes the late arrival. Lincoln Square staffs its desk only from 7:00 a.m. to 11:00 p.m. It can arrange an after-hours key pickup, but the hotel requires advance coordination and does not guarantee that arrangement until the day of arrival.
That is not ideal. What about payment and cancellation at Fairfield? I saw two prices.

The $711 total is guaranteed by card but paid at the hotel. It allows cancellation without penalty through September 23 at 11:59 p.m. Chicago time; after that, the penalty is the full stay. The lower $674 total is an advance-purchase rate. The hotel charges it on September 20, and it becomes nonrefundable once charged.

Its $624 total is also card-guaranteed and paid at the property. Cancellation is free through September 21 at 6:00 p.m. Chicago time, followed by a one-night room-and-tax penalty. The after-hours arrival arrangement is separate from the cancellation terms.
Please verify Monday storage specifically. We need to check out early, leave both bags, and collect them before taking the Blue Line to O’Hare.

Fairfield confirms complimentary luggage storage for registered guests on checkout day, handled at the staffed front desk. Both standard suitcases can be left after an early checkout and collected around 10:15 a.m. Lincoln Square will hold bags only during desk hours and says space is subject to availability, so it would not guarantee storage in advance.
Does staying downtown still work for Saturday dinner and Sunday’s museum time?

Yes. Leave Fairfield around 4:55 p.m. Saturday for the Red and Brown Lines to Western, reaching the 6:00 p.m. Lincoln Square dinner with a useful margin. On Sunday, leave around 9:55 a.m. and reach the Art Institute near 10:15 for the 10:30 entry. Monday, retrieve the bags at 10:15, leave by about 10:25, and take the Blue Line to O’Hare for the 1:50 p.m. flight.
Book the Fairfield refundable rate, one shared king room for all three nights. Add the late-arrival note and do not use the advance-purchase option.

The Fairfield Inn & Suites Chicago Downtown/River North is confirmed for September 25–28: one king room for two adults, three nights, confirmation FCR-925731. The total is $711 including taxes, guaranteed by card and payable at the hotel. Free cancellation runs through September 23 at 11:59 p.m. Chicago time. I added the late-arrival note for approximately 11:15–11:35 p.m. and confirmed complimentary Monday luggage storage. With the $642 flights and $30 estimated CTA cost, the working trip total is now $1,383.
